Title: WEB-INF directory exclusion bypass in webResources routing plugin (jakarta)
Analysis:
The `webResources` routing plugin in Ktor servlet-jakarta suffers from the exact same security vulnerability as the standard servlet plugin. It tries to block requests to the sensitive `WEB-INF` directory by adding an exclusion predicate: `path == "WEB-INF" || path.startsWith("WEB-INF/")`. However, when constructing the path to match against the exclusions, it prepends a leading slash: `val path = (prefix + filteredPath).joinToString("/", prefix = "/")`. When the default `subPath = "/"` is used, the prefix is empty, resulting in `path` starting with a leading slash (e.g. `"/WEB-INF/web.xml"`). Since the string starts with `"/"`, the exclusion `path.startsWith("WEB-INF/")` evaluates to `false`, allowing attackers to bypass the check and retrieve sensitive servlet container files (like `web.xml`, compilation classes, libraries, and credentials) via programmatic resource resolution (`ServletContext.getResource`).

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
Make a GET request to a route utilizing `webResources` (e.g., mounted at `/static` or root):
`GET /static/WEB-INF/web.xml HTTP/1.1`
The path parameter will resolve to `["WEB-INF", "web.xml"]`, joining to `"/WEB-INF/web.xml"`. The `excludes` filter evaluates `"/WEB-INF/web.xml".startsWith("WEB-INF/")`, which is false. The request then proceeds to load the file via `ServletContext.getResource("/WEB-INF/web.xml")` and returns it to the client.
